options: Microsoft's procedural extension of standard SQL, built into SQL Server
A separate database engine that replaces SQL Server
A visual, drag-and-drop query builder
A cloud-only version of SQL that doesn't run on-premises
questions.explain: T-SQL adds procedural features — variables, control-of-flow, error handling, transactions — on top of standard SQL's core vocabulary.

questions.q: What is SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)?
options: Microsoft's free integrated environment for writing and running T-SQL
A paid add-on required to connect to SQL Server
A reporting tool for building dashboards
The name of the AdventureWorks sample database
questions.explain: SSMS is free and is where this entire course's queries get written and executed.

questions.q: Which SSMS panel shows a tree of your servers, databases, and their tables?
options: Object Explorer
Query Editor
Results grid
Messages tab
questions.explain: Object Explorer is the browsable tree of everything you have access to on the connected server.

questions.q: How do you run a query in SSMS?
options: Click Execute on the toolbar, or press F5
Save the file and restart SSMS
Right-click Object Explorer and choose Run
Queries run automatically as you type
questions.explain: Execute (or the F5 shortcut) sends the current Query Editor contents to the connected server.

questions.q: Which two sample databases does this course use, and for what?
options: AdventureWorks2012 for Chapters 1–11 (OLTP); AdventureWorksDW2014 for Chapter 12 (data warehouse)
Northwind for every chapter
AdventureWorksDW2014 for Chapters 1–11; AdventureWorks2012 for Chapter 12
A different invented database for every chapter
questions.explain: AdventureWorks2012 is the transactional (OLTP) database used throughout most of the course; AdventureWorksDW2014 is the pre-built data warehouse used in the final chapter on warehousing concepts.
